subtitle: Your photo library, on your own server
description:
Roll keeps your photos on a timeline of the days you took them, by the camera's own clock. Each month and day has a heading with its place, and the days flow along rows that fill the screen. A date rail jumps through the years, and a pinch makes the photos bigger or smaller.

On this day brings back photos from today's date in earlier years, as a short story that drifts from one photo to the next.

Drop photos anywhere, choose them or paste them. Roll reads each one's date, camera, exposure and location in your browser, names the place without asking any service, skips photos it already has, and keeps the original. The viewer grows out of the photo you tap, swipes and zooms, and shows the details beside the photo.

Collect photos into albums and share one by link: anyone with it sees the album, no account needed, without places, cameras or file names. Places, favourites, a Trash that waits 30 days, and search over places, cameras, months and more.

It feels like an app: frosted bars that stay put, a tab bar on your phone and a sidebar on a desk, light and dark, with photos on black.
whatsNew: A slightly wider sidebar, so its footer line no longer breaks in two.
